title: Improve mobile keyboard scrolling and tool accordions
Research current mobile layout, scrolling, and tool call rendering
Implement keyboard-aware composer and robust bottom stickiness controls
Implement per-tool-call argument/output accordions collapsed by default

content: Starting research on the current React Native mobile layout, scroll behavior, and tool call rendering before making UI changes.

observation: Development should stay simple, use focused tests where practical, and prefer small intention-revealing helpers over complex defensive UI code.

The mobile app is an Expo/React Native iPhone-first MVP with a session timeline, bottom composer, TUI-style working spinner, and fully expanded tool arguments/output today. Physical phones need LAN host URLs, but the requested changes are client-side UI behavior.

SessionScreen currently renders a plain View containing header, FlatList timeline, optional WorkingIndicator, and Composer; there is no KeyboardAvoidingView, no auto-scroll/pin state, and no floating jump-to-bottom control.

Tool cards are rendered through BashToolCard, ReadToolCard, and GenericToolCard. Arguments and output are displayed by ToolArguments/PlainToolOutput/ReadToolOutput through ToolSection, which is always expanded today.
Timeline tool items have stable ids plus args/detail fields; streaming text updates preserve timeline item ids, so per-row local UI state can remain isolated when FlatList rows keep the same key.
The screenshot shows the iOS keyboard covering the bottom composer area, confirming the session screen needs keyboard-aware layout rather than only timeline/content styling.

content: Research complete. The implementation can be done within the Expo app without protocol changes: wrap the session layout in keyboard avoidance, add tested bottom-stickiness helpers wired to FlatList scroll events, and convert existing ToolSection rendering into per-section accordions collapsed by default.
